episodes.210764: Multiple segments of heavy showers and a few thunderstorms moved across north Alabama during the evening hours.  One segment moved northeast during the late evening from central into northeast Alabama which exhibited a bow echo. This resulted in a power pole being snapped and trees being knocked down in Jackson and Marshall Counties.  A couple of trees were also knocked down blocking roads in Lauderdale and Morgan Counties.
episodes.210777: A cold front draped from the Middle Atlantic into the western portions of North Carolina during the morning hours pushed east and southeast during the evening hours. Ahead of the cold front, isolated to scattered showers and storms raced ahead of the front and produced some isolated wind damage across Halifax County during the early afternoon hours.
episodes.210788: Storms formed a broken line along a cold front in an unseasonably warm airmass.
episodes.210890: A cold front was accompanied by a narrow band of heavier squalls embedded within a larger area of light to moderate stratiform rain. These squalls resulted in several gale-force wind gusts as the front crossed the waters.
episodes.212202: A cold front moved across Southeast Michigan during the late afternoon and early evening of April 4. This triggered two lines of thunderstorms that caused pockets of damage south of I-94. The most significant storm occurred in Wayne County, producing an EF-1 tornado in Van Buren Township. The system also dumped 1 to 3 inches of rain, with some areas seeing up to 4 inches. Because the region had already received 3 to 5 inches over the previous five days, these additional downpours caused the Tittabawassee, Clinton, and Flint rivers to overflow. In addition, significant localized flooding occurred on already saturated ground, with the hardest-hit area being northwest Oakland County, specifically in and around Holly.
episodes.212539: A cold front moved across Virginia on April 5, 2026. A weak surface low along the cold front helped produce a line of severe storms across southeast Virginia.
episodes.212540: A cold front moved across the Mid-Atlantic on April 5, 2026. A line of storms developed ahead of the front and produced gusty winds across the Chesapeake Bay, Currituck Sound, Virginia coastal waters, James River, and York River.
episodes.212690: A surface trough developed across the Coastal Plain during the afternoon hours of Sunday April fifth out ahead of an eastward moving cold front. An ongoing line of scattered showers and thunderstorms quickly tracked east from central North Carolina to the coast and strengthened as they interacted with the surface trough in the coastal plain with a few of these storms becoming strong in nature bringing strong and damaging winds to portions of the northern sounds and Pamlico river.
episodes.212812: In the afternoon hours of April 4 and 5, reports indicated the presence of waterspouts across the local waters to the north and southeast of Puerto Rico.
episodes.213078: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front on the afternoon of April 5, 2026.
episodes.213195: A cold front approached the region from the west on April 4th while a warm and moist airmass remained in place across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi. Moisture continued to increase through the day, with numerous showers and thunderstorms developing ahead of the front, especially across the western half of the forecast area. The strongest convection moved across West Feliciana Parish during the evening and produced heavy rainfall over a short period of time. While the overall severe weather threat was limited, repeated storms and locally heavy downpours led to flash flooding in parts of the parish.
episodes.213196: A cold front approached the region from the west on April 4th and 5th while a warm and moist airmass remained in place across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi. Moisture continued to increase ahead of the approaching frontal boundary, which fueled the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms. The strongest convection moved across southwest Mississippi during the early morning hours of April 5th and produced heavy rainfall over a short period of time. While the overall severe weather threat was limited, repeated storms and locally heavy downpours led to flash flooding in parts of Pike County.
episodes.213532: With high pressure over the region, an isolated line of convection developed along the leading edge of the area of rain. This line produced damaging winds in the Lake Cumberland area of Kentucky.
